item.title: Two arrested after stolen truck, trailers lead to multiple pursuits across Mississippi, Alabama - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GEORGE COUNTY – Two people have been arrested following multiple theft investigations and vehicle pursuits involving stolen property in George County and Mobile County, Alabama.

According to the George County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were investigating a possible stolen vehicle May 24 in the Agricola area of George County when they saw the vehicle being driven by Charles Mott. Deputies attempted to stop the vehicle for traffic violations, but the vehicle fled into Alabama.

A few hours later, Mobile County deputies saw the vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, which led to another pursuit. Authorities said the pursuit continued until the vehicle came back into Greene County, Mississippi, where it ended. The vehicle was not recovered at that time.

On May 26, the George County Sheriff’s Office received a report of a stolen travel trailer from the Rocky Creek area. Investigators learned the trailer was at Mott’s property in Agricola. Investigators went to the property and confirmed through the VIN that it was the stolen trailer from Rocky Creek.

While investigators were recovering the stolen camper trailer, other George County deputies saw the previously stolen truck, which had been painted a different color, towing a large flatbed trailer in the Howell area of George County. Authorities said Mott was driving the vehicle, and Stephanie Valentine was also inside.

Deputies attempted another traffic stop, but the suspects again fled into Mobile County, Alabama. Mobile County authorities later saw the vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, which led to another pursuit. Mobile County deputies were ultimately able to stop the vehicle and arrest Mott and Valentine without further incident.

Both are being held at the Mobile County Metro Jail.

Mott is facing charges in Mobile County, Alabama, including first-degree robbery, first-degree receiving stolen property, felony attempt to elude, three counts of first-degree criminal mischief, three counts of second-degree assault and fugitive from justice in Mississippi.

Valentine is facing charges in Mobile County, including first-degree robbery, second-degree possession of marijuana, possession of drug paraphernalia, second-degree elder abuse and fugitive from justice in Mississippi.

On May 27, the George County Sheriff’s Office received a report of a stolen flatbed trailer from the Shipman area. Deputies identified the trailer as the same one being towed by Mott during the May 26 pursuit.

On May 28, the George County Criminal Investigation Division received information about the trailer’s location in the Semmes, Alabama, area. The trailer has since been recovered.

The George County Sheriff’s Office has placed holds on Mott for motor vehicle theft, grand larceny of a camper trailer, grand larceny of a flatbed trailer and felony fleeing.

Valentine has holds for grand larceny of a camper trailer and grand larceny of a flatbed trailer.

“These individuals demonstrated a blatant disregard for the law and the safety of others by repeatedly fleeing from law enforcement,” Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said. “Let this serve as a reminder that the George County Sheriff’s Office will continue pressing forward to hold accountable those who commit crimes in our community, regardless of where they attempt to flee.”

Mixon commended George County deputies, investigators and dispatchers, along with the Mobile County Sheriff’s Office, for helping apprehend the suspects and recover the stolen property.

All suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

item.title: Tunica Humane Society issues warning about leaving children and pets in vehicles - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – The Tunica Humane Society is warning the public about the dangers of leaving pets unattended inside vehicles as temperatures continue to rise.

In a recent social media post, the organization stressed that temperatures inside a vehicle can increase rapidly and become deadly in a matter of minutes.

According to the post, if the outside temperature is 85 degrees, the temperature inside a vehicle can climb to 104 degrees within 10 minutes.

The humane society urged the public to never leave children or pets inside a parked vehicle, even for a short trip into a store.

Officials said the risk increases the longer a person or animal remains inside the vehicle.

item.title: Silver Alert issued for missing Lowndes County man last seen in Lauderdale County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
LAUDERDALE COUNTY — A Silver Alert has been issued for a missing Lowndes County man believed to be driving in east Mississippi.

Robert Glen Banks, 62, of Caledonia, was last seen around 11:34 p.m. Wednesday in the area of Causeyville Road in Lauderdale County traveling north.

Banks is believed to be driving a 2006 Lexus ES350 bearing Mississippi tag DB4712E.

Family members said Banks suffers from a medical condition that may impair his judgment.

Banks is 5 feet, 11 inches tall, weighs about 146 pounds, with white hair and brown eyes.

Anyone who sees Banks or the vehicle is asked to call the Lowndes County Sheriff’s Department at 1-800-530-7151 or call 911.

item.title: Scott County deputies, MBN seize drugs, guns and vehicles in searches - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
SCOTT COUNTY – Two men were charged after law enforcement agencies executed separate search warrants in Scott County and Lake.

According to officials, the Scott County Sheriff’s Office Narcotics Task Force and the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics executed a search warrant May 27 at the home of Alvester Tucker at 1213 E. Oak St. in Forest.

During the search, authorities seized about 28 grams of methamphetamine, narcotics distribution scales, multiple firearms, two vehicles and currency believed to be from illegal narcotics sales.

A separate search warrant was executed at the home of Rodney Mitchell on Thornton Street in Lake by the Scott County Sheriff’s Office Narcotics Task Force, the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics and the Lake Police Department.

Authorities said that search led to the seizure of about 5 grams of methamphetamine, 0.5 grams of crack cocaine and other items commonly used in the distribution of illegal narcotics.

Tucker has been charged with possession of methamphetamine.

Mitchell has been charged with possession of methamphetamine, sale of methamphetamine, possession of cocaine and possession of a firearm by a felon.

Officials said the searches were the result of a joint investigation between the agencies.

item.title: Natchez man arrested on Alabama fugitive warrant - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – A Natchez man was arrested Thursday on a fugitive warrant out of Alabama, according to the Adams County Sheriff’s Office.

Deputies arrested 33-year-old John Brandon Sanders, of Natchez, on May 28 after responding to a residence on Kingston Road.

According to the incident report, deputies received information about an NCIC hit connected to Sanders. After confirming the warrant with Baldwin County, Alabama, authorities, Sanders was taken into custody without incident.

He was transported to the Adams County Sheriff’s Office for booking.

Authorities said the Baldwin County warrant is for a probation revocation connected to an original charge of first-degree rape. Court documents indicate the warrant carries no bond and is listed for extradition within several southeastern states, including Mississippi and Alabama.

Sanders is being held pending extradition proceedings.

All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

item.title: Jackson police searching for man accused in fraudulent vehicle title scheme - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Jackson Police Department is searching for a man accused of conspiring to fraudulently transfer ownership of a vehicle using forged documents.

Police said Adarius Bounds is wanted on a conspiracy charge connected to an alleged scheme involving a fraudulent power of attorney.

Investigators allege Bounds conspired with his sister, Yamonique Bounds, who has already been arrested, to obtain a fraudulent power of attorney document in order to transfer the title of a vehicle from its owner to himself.

Authorities said the forged document, which allegedly included the vehicle owner’s forged signature, was presented to the Mississippi Department of Revenue to obtain a new title.

After the title was obtained, police said Bounds sold the vehicle to another person.

Anyone with information about Bounds’ whereabouts is asked to contact Jackson police at 601-960-1800 or Crime Stoppers of Central Mississippi at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: Former Olive Branch teacher sentenced to 25 years in child exploitation case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
OLIVE BRANCH – Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced that a former Olive Branch teacher and preacher has been sentenced in a child exploitation case stemming from a 2023 undercover operation.

Former Olive Branch Pastor/Teacher Charged With Child Exploitation

According to the Attorney General’s Office, 32-year-old Kyle Michael Hilleary of Olive Branch was convicted on one count of child exploitation following a jury trial. The case was investigated and prosecuted by the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office with assistance from the Olive Branch Police Department. Authorities said the investigation originated from “Operation Toil and Trouble,” an undercover operation conducted in 2023.

On May 26, 2026, 23rd Circuit Court Judge Celeste Wilson sentenced Hilleary to 35 years, with 25 years to serve day-for-day without the possibility of parole in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections. He was also sentenced to five years of probation.

In addition, Hilleary was ordered to pay $1,000 to the Victims of Human Trafficking and Commercial Sexual Exploitation Fund and $1,000 to the Mississippi Children’s Trust Fund. He is also required to register as a sex offender.

“These crimes rob a child of their innocence and the images can cause a lifetime of trauma, re-victimizing the child over and over again,” Attorney General Lynn Fitch said in a statement. “And when the perpetrator is someone in a position of authority, they violate a covenant with the parents who entrusted them with their children. We will not tolerate such abuse.”

Officials encouraged anyone with information about online child sexual exploitation to contact the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children at 1-800-843-5678 or submit a report online at cybertipline.org.

item.title: Florida men sentenced in Madison Burn Boot Camp burglary spree - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MADISON — Two Florida men have been sentenced to decades in prison for their roles in a series of vehicle burglaries targeting women attending an early morning workout class at a Madison fitness center, prosecutors said.

Madison and Rankin Counties District Attorney John K. “Bubba” Bramlett announced that Victor Andrew Ogiste, 29, and Ramone Davis, 31, both of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, were convicted in connection with a string of auto burglaries at Burn Boot Camp in Madison in October 2023.

Ogiste was sentenced to 35 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections without the possibility of parole or early release after being sentenced as a habitual offender. Davis received a 40-year sentence with the possibility of parole.

According to investigators, Madison police responded Oct. 13, 2023, after multiple vehicles were burglarized during a 5 a.m. workout class at Burn Boot Camp. Officers said an individual smashed windows on 11 vehicles in about 20 minutes, stealing purses, wallets, credit cards and other personal items before fleeing in a 2022 Toyota RAV4.

Surveillance footage allowed officers to identify the vehicle and enter its tag number into a license plate reader system. Investigators later learned a similar burglary had occurred two days earlier at a Burn Boot Camp location in Oxford.

The investigation led officers to a rented Airbnb in Hattiesburg, where investigators from the Madison Police Department and Forrest County Sheriff’s Office executed search warrants and recovered stolen property from the Madison and Oxford burglaries, including credit cards, driver’s licenses and other personal belongings.

Authorities later tracked the suspects to Alabama after learning they were traveling in a Chrysler 300. Officers in Trussville conducted a traffic stop, identifying Ogiste as the driver and Davis as a passenger.

Investigators analyzed several cell phones recovered from the vehicle and found evidence placing both men at the Madison burglary scene. Prosecutors said Ogiste had searched online for Burn Boot Camp locations, and geolocation data showed both defendants traveling from Fort Lauderdale through multiple states before arriving in Mississippi.

Ogiste failed to appear for trial and was tried in absentia in September 2025. A Madison County jury convicted him on 11 counts of auto burglary and one count of conspiracy. U.S. Marshals later arrested him in Fort Worth, Texas, in December 2025.

Davis also failed to appear for court but was later arrested and pleaded guilty to five burglary counts and one count of conspiracy.

Bramlett praised the multi-agency investigation and said modern investigative tools, including GPS and cell phone data, played a major role in securing the convictions.

item.title: Donations pour in for Hattiesburg therapist after wife killed in Petal flash flooding - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
HATTIESBURG — Friends and supporters are rallying around a Hattiesburg family after a local therapist battling brain cancer lost his wife in a flash flood tragedy over Memorial Day weekend.

A GoFundMe created for Ben Floyd has seen an outpouring of support following the death of his wife, Rachael Floyd, who organizers say was killed May 25 during a flash flood incident in Petal.

The fundraiser was originally launched after Ben Floyd was diagnosed with a high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features, an aggressive form of brain cancer located in the cerebellum. Organizers said Floyd, who is self-employed as a therapist in Hattiesburg, has been unable to work regularly while undergoing treatment.

Following Rachael Floyd’s sudden death, organizers updated the fundraiser to state that donations will now help Ben Floyd care for the couple’s three young sons while navigating both his medical battle and the loss of his wife.

Supporters described Floyd as a compassionate counselor, devoted father and active member of the community who has spent years helping others through personal crises and hardships.

The couple’s children are Joshua, 4, Gilead, 2, and Mayhew, 1, according to the fundraiser page.

Organizers said additional information about funeral arrangements for Rachael Floyd is expected to be announced later.

item.title: UMMC AirCare expands fleet with addition of fixed-wing aircraft - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Rachel Vanderford University of Mississippi Medical Center

JACKSON – The University of Mississippi Medical Center AirCare flight team is preparing to expand its fleet with the addition of a fixed-wing aircraft and is looking to hire 10 additional medical staff members to support the new service.

The aircraft, a Pilatus PC-12 provided through UMMC’s partnership with Global Medical Response, will become the fifth vehicle in the AirCare fleet, expanding the program’s ability to provide in-state and regional patient transport.

“Adding a fixed-wing aircraft is a natural evolution for AirCare and gives us another tool to serve patients across Mississippi and the surrounding region,” said Jeremy Benson, director of the Mississippi Center for Emergency Services, and program director for AirCare – Helicopter Transport. “It allows us to move patients safely and efficiently over longer distances, particularly when rotor-wing transport may not be the most practical option.”

item.title: Two Baldwyn men arrested after deputies respond to burglary in progress - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PRENTISS COUNTY – Two Baldwyn men were arrested after deputies responded to a burglary in progress at a Prentiss County home.

According to the Prentiss County Sheriff’s Office, deputies were dispatched around 9:34 a.m. May 22 to a residence at 20 County Road 5075.

Deputies Navarro and Lawson met with the homeowner’s sister, who said two men had forced their way into her brother’s home. She told deputies she saw the suspects on security camera footage and that both men ran into the woods behind the home when she arrived.

The suspects were described as shirtless, with one wearing black shorts and the other wearing brown pants.

Deputies spotted two people matching the description running along the property line. Both were taken into custody without incident and identified as 29-year-old Jacob Wayne Mears and 37-year-old Aaron Eddie Kelly, both of Baldwyn.

Deputies said a search of the suspects found multiple items belonging to the homeowner. A large amount of methamphetamine was also found near the suspects where they were taken into custody.

The homeowner told deputies items had also been removed from a disabled vehicle on the property and placed into a 2008 GMC Sierra registered to Mears. The truck was backed into the driveway with a trailer loaded with appliances, according to the sheriff’s office.

A .22 revolver found on the trailer was also recovered and identified by the homeowner as having been taken from under his bed.

Authorities said security camera images showed both suspects entering and leaving the residence.

Mears was charged with burglary of a dwelling, burglary of an automobile and possession of methamphetamine, 10 to 30 grams, enhanced with a firearm.

Kelly was charged with burglary of a dwelling, burglary of an automobile, possession of a weapon by a felon, possession of methamphetamine, 10 to 30 grams, enhanced with a firearm, and tampering with physical evidence. Authorities said all charges against Kelly will be pursued under habitual offender status.

Both suspects are currently under supervision by the Mississippi Department of Corrections, according to the sheriff’s office.

Justice Court Judge Ray Hall set Mears’ bond at $150,000 and Kelly’s bond at $200,000.

Both men were taken to the Prentiss County Jail. The charges will be presented to a Prentiss County grand jury.

item.title: Senatobia Public Library to host local author festival June 6 - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
SENATOBIA — Readers will have a chance to meet Mississippi authors, purchase signed books and hear the stories behind their work during the upcoming Author Fest at the Senatobia Public Library on June 6.

The event will feature authors published through Rose & Pearl Publishing and showcase a variety of genres ranging from faith-based books and memoirs to children’s literature and Southern fiction.

Featured authors include Pat Hardison, author of “Facing the Fire”; Troy Day, author of “The Fruit”; Chilly Billy Howell, author of “Wrestling with Wisdom at the Crossroads”; and Heather Burchfield, author of “Not Here to Be Nice.”

Other featured works include “Floating Thoughts” by Candy Warren, “First Steps of Faith” by Carolyn Wiley and Candy Warren, and the children’s book “Who Am I When No One is Around?”

Organizers said the festival is intended to celebrate local storytelling and connect readers with authors from their own communities.

The event will take place June 6 at the Senatobia Public Library.

item.title: Pike County jury convicts McComb man on sexual battery charges involving child - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
PIKE COUNTY — A Pike County jury found a McComb man guilty Tuesday on charges of sexual battery and touching a child for lustful purposes following a one-day trial in Circuit Court.

According to prosecutors, Calvin Rasheed Patterson, 34, was convicted on one count of sexual battery and one count of touching and handling a child for lustful purposes.

The charges stemmed from an investigation launched after the victim came forward in 2024 and reported that Patterson assaulted her in July of that year. Prosecutors said the victim, now 15 years old, testified before the jury about the abuse.

Following the verdict, Circuit Judge Michael Taylor sentenced Patterson to 25 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections to be served day for day. Patterson will also be required to register as a sex offender.

“I want to thank the McComb Police Department, and the nursing staff at Southwest Mississippi Regional Medical Center for all of their hard work and continuing investigation into such serious crimes. We continue to have young people come forward and describe the abuse that they have been subjected to. Our office will continue to work to protect our youth from predators that choose harm the most vulnerable of our community. Joey and Sebastian did an outstanding job and worked tirelessly to get justice for this young lady and hold Patterson accountable for his actions. I am proud of my team and how brave this young lady was in coming forward and sharing her story,” said District Attorney Brendon Adams.

Assistant District Attorneys Sebastian Harrell and Joey Norton prosecuted the case.

item.title: Mississippi Magnolia Gardens seeks donations to expand memorial tribute space - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A memorial garden at the Mississippi Agriculture and Forestry Museum is giving Mississippians a way to honor loved ones while helping preserve a decades-old tradition rooted in the state’s history.

The Mississippi Magnolia Gardens, located on the museum grounds in Jackson, allows donors to dedicate gifts in honor or memory of individuals and organizations through contributions supporting the garden’s continued growth and maintenance.

Officials with the Mississippi Agriculture and Forestry Museum Foundation said donations begin at $75 and help fund landscaping, plantings and long-term improvements to the garden space, which includes magnolia trees, walkways and gathering areas designed for reflection and remembrance.

The project continues the legacy of Mississippi’s former “Avenue of Magnolias,” a longtime statewide program that allowed families to honor loved ones through magnolia tree plantings. The current Magnolia Gardens opened in 2021, approximately 60 years after the original tradition began.

Foundation leaders said more than $100,000 in donations helped complete the initial phase of the gardens, but another $150,000 is needed to fully complete the planned vision for the site.

“The Mississippi Magnolia Gardens is more than a garden; it is a storybook of Mississippi families, memories, and milestones,” Foundation Board Chair Dr. Bill Herndon said. “Every donation helps ensure this tradition continues for generations to come.”

According to the foundation, each donation is acknowledged with a letter, and honorees or family members designated by donors also receive notification of the tribute.

The gardens are open year-round during regular museum hours.

Additional information and donation opportunities are available through the Mississippi Agriculture and Forestry Museum Foundation.

item.title: Millsaps agrees to cover at least half of tuition for eligible JPS students - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Eligible Jackson Public Schools students will now be able to attend Millsaps College with at least half of their tuition covered under a new partnership announced Tuesday.

The agreement, finalized through a memorandum of understanding between the two institutions, provides renewable undergraduate scholarships covering at least 50% of tuition for JPS students who meet Millsaps’ standard admissions requirements. The scholarships may be renewed for up to four years.

Millsaps officials said the initiative is designed to help more Jackson students pursue higher education locally while creating a stronger long-term workforce pipeline within Mississippi.

“Mississippi’s future depends on our ability to educate, retain and empower homegrown talent,” Millsaps President Frank Neville said in a statement. “This partnership creates a clear pathway for Jackson students and families to see a future for themselves right here.”

The agreement also extends benefits to Jackson Public Schools employees and families. Dependents of full-time JPS faculty and staff will also qualify for the undergraduate tuition scholarship.

Additionally, full-time JPS employees, parents of current students and JPS alumni may receive a 10% tuition discount on select graduate programs offered through the Else School of Management at Millsaps.

JPS Superintendent Errick L. Greene said the partnership expands opportunities for students preparing for careers and higher education.

“This partnership with Millsaps College will help bring that vision to life,” Greene said.

Officials said the agreement will remain in effect for five years and includes outreach efforts such as campus visits and recruitment programs aimed at helping students explore college and career opportunities earlier.

item.title: MDWFP urges residents to be BearWise as black bears move across Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks is reminding residents to take precautions as black bears move across the state during early summer.

The Hinds County Sheriff’s Department shared a recent sighting of black bears in Utica on Memorial Day.

Black bears spotted near Utica on Memorial Day, sheriff says

According to MDWFP, young black bears, especially males, often travel long distances this time of year while searching for new territory. Black bears typically stay with their mother for the first 16 to 18 months of life before venturing out on their own.

Officials said the roaming behavior is normal, but bears may pass through towns and neighborhoods, especially when attracted by easy food sources.

To help reduce conflicts and keep people and bears safe, MDWFP is encouraging residents to secure trash and compost, put away pet food, store bird feeders and clean and secure grills and smokers.

Residents are also encouraged to notify neighbors if a bear is seen nearby so others can take precautions.

MDWFP said people should never approach or feed bears. Photos and videos should only be taken from a safe distance.

Bear sightings may be reported through MDWFP’s website at mdwfp.com.

item.title: UPDATE: Carly Gregg's attorney urges Mississippi Supreme Court to vacate life sentence - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
UPDATE:

JACKSON — Attorneys for Carly Gregg argued before the Mississippi Supreme Court on Tuesday that her first-degree murder conviction and life sentence in the shooting death of her mother should be thrown out, contending the trial moved too quickly to allow a fair sentencing hearing for a juvenile offender.

Defense attorney James H. Murphy told the court the entire case, from the March 19, 2024, shooting in Rankin County to Gregg’s sentencing on Sept. 20, 2024, proceeded in 183 days, a pace he called “extraordinary” for a case involving complex psychiatric evidence and questions of dissociation tied to psychotropic medication. The court pushed back, asking if it wasn’t one of the charges of the system to give a speedy trial.

Gregg was 14 when she shot and killed her mother, Ashley Smylie, and wounded her stepfather, Heath Smylie, at the family’s Brandon home. A jury convicted her of first-degree murder and attempted first-degree murder and sentenced her to life imprisonment.

Much of Tuesday’s argument focused on what Gregg’s life sentence actually means under Mississippi law. The Legislature amended the first-degree murder sentencing statute effective July 1, 2024, adding a juvenile-specific sentencing structure. The subsection which addresses capital murder gives juries the option of life imprisonment or life without the possibility of parole, while the subsection which governs first-degree murder and applies to Gregg lists only life imprisonment.

Murphy argued that because the Legislature expressly included “life without parole” as an option for capital murder but left it out for first-degree murder, a juvenile convicted of first-degree murder cannot legally be sentenced to life without parole.

Justices pressed Special Assistant Attorney General Allison Hartman on the same point. Hartman argued that under the court’s 2024 decision in Johnson v. State, the sentencing statute must be read together with the state’s parole eligibility statute, which bars parole for those convicted of first-degree murder. The result, she said, is that life imprisonment is effectively life without parole.

One justice questioned that reading, noting the sentencing order itself says only “life imprisonment” and observing that if the Legislature later changed the parole statute, defendants would have to be resentenced. Another justice pointed to the difference between the two subsections, asking why the Legislature would spell out “life without parole” as a separate option for capital murder if it intended the same outcome for first-degree murder.

Murphy said the defense would concede the issue if the court interpreted the amendment to mean Gregg’s life sentence carries the possibility of parole.

On the Miller v. Alabama framework, which requires an individualized sentencing hearing before a juvenile can be sentenced to die in prison, Murphy argued the hearing in Gregg’s case fell short. After the jury returned its verdict, both sides rested on the evidence already presented and went straight to closing argument, he said. item.title: George County juveniles charged after beer can shatters deputy’s windshield - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GEORGE COUNTY – Two juveniles were charged after a reckless driving call led to a patrol unit’s windshield being shattered in George County.

According to the George County Sheriff’s Office, deputies responded to a call about a reckless driver in the area of Sally Parker Road. While patrolling the area, a responding deputy saw a vehicle matching the caller’s description.

As the deputy passed the vehicle, someone threw an object from it, later identified as a beer can, officials said. The beer can struck the patrol unit and shattered the front windshield.

The vehicle was later stopped without further incident.

Deputies said they had also received reports before the reckless driving call of a vehicle striking mailboxes in the River Road area. Investigators believe the incidents are related.

The two occupants of the vehicle were identified as juveniles. Their names will not be released because of their ages.

After further investigation, the driver was charged with DUI, two counts of malicious mischief, minor in possession of alcohol, littering, petit larceny and no proof of insurance.

The juvenile passenger was charged with minor in possession of alcohol.

“This type of reckless and dangerous behavior will not be tolerated,” Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said. “Throwing objects at vehicles endangers our deputies and the public. We are committed to holding those responsible fully accountable.”

The investigation remains active, and additional charges may be forthcoming.

Anyone with additional information is asked to contact the George County Sheriff’s Office.

item.title: Florence man sentenced to 15 years in child exploitation case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
FLORENCE – A Florence man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after being convicted on two counts of child exploitation, Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced.

According to Fitch’s office, Kevin Wayne Owen, 47, was sentenced May 19 by Rankin County Circuit Court Judge Dewey Arthur.

Owen was sentenced to 40 years, with 15 years to serve day for day without the possibility of parole in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections. He will also serve 25 years on probation.

Fitch’s office said the case was investigated and prosecuted by the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office and began through an undercover operation.

“Our team of investigators and prosecutors at the Attorney General’s Office is committed to protecting our children and making the Internet a safer place,” Fitch said. “AGO investigators uncovered Owen’s cache of child sex abuse material and the secret cameras he used to create it pursuant to an undercover operation and AGO prosecutors took the case to court. We will always seek justice for our children.”

Owen was ordered to pay $1,000 to the Victims of Human Trafficking and Commercial Sexual Exploitation Fund, $1,000 to the Mississippi Children’s Trust Fund and $1,000 to the Mississippi Crime Victim Compensation Fund.

He must also register as a sex offender.

Anyone with information about a child being sexually exploited online is asked to report it to 1-800-843-5678 or online at cybertipline.org. The hotline is operated by the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

item.title: Clinton officials issue gross but important reminder: Stop flushing wipes - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CLINTON – City of Clinton officials are reminding residents that “flushable” wipes should not be flushed after a large buildup was found in the city’s sewer system.

According to the city, a photo taken from the sewer system showed a large buildup of wipes mixed with fats, oils and grease.

Officials said although some wipes are labeled as flushable, they do not break down like toilet paper and can cause serious blockages in sewer lines and pumps.

The city said grease, cooking oil and fats poured down drains can combine with wipes and other debris, creating large clogs that may damage equipment, back up sewer lines and lead to costly repairs for homeowners and the city.

Officials said the cost of maintaining and repairing damaged sewer infrastructure can also contribute to increased sewer rates over time.

Residents are asked not to flush wipes, even if the package says they are flushable. Officials are also reminding residents not to pour grease, fats or cooking oils down the drain and to only flush toilet paper.

The city said a few seconds of prevention at home can help prevent expensive problems for the entire community.

item.title: Carroll County man jailed after deputies find fully automatic firearm during traffic stop - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CARROLL COUNTY — A Carroll County man is facing multiple felony charges after deputies said they discovered a firearm converted to fully automatic during a weekend traffic stop.

According to the Carroll County Sheriff’s Office, deputies stopped a vehicle Sunday night on Highway 82 near Valley Hill and conducted a search of the vehicle.

During the search, deputies reportedly found a firearm equipped with a machine gun conversion device, making the weapon fully automatic.

Authorities arrested Jaquaveous Swims, 24, of the Carrollton area. He was booked into the Carroll County Regional Correctional Facility and charged with possession of a firearm by a felon, possession of a stolen firearm and possession of a machine gun conversion device.

Swims remained jailed as of Tuesday.

Sheriff Clint Walker said the department takes a “hardline stance” against illegal firearm possession by convicted felons and praised deputies for their work during the stop.

item.title: 19-year-old wanted after two men found shot to death in Tunica County neighborhood - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – A 19-year-old Tunica man is wanted for questioning after two men were found shot to death in a Tunica County subdivision.

According to the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office, deputies received a 911 call around 7:37 p.m. Sunday, May 24, reporting that someone had hit a tree and appeared to be unresponsive in the White Oak subdivision.

When deputies arrived, they found that both people had been shot.

The victims were identified as 42-year-old Taurean Martez Thomas and 33-year-old David Brown III, both of Tunica. Both men were pronounced dead at the scene by the Tunica County coroner.

The sheriff’s office said 19-year-old Jadarius Antwan Douglas, of Tunica, is wanted for questioning in the double homicide.

The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office Criminal Investigation Division has also obtained warrants for Douglas in connection with additional crimes. Authorities said the warrants include two counts of kidnapping, armed robbery, simple assault and shooting into a motor vehicle.

Officials said it has not been confirmed whether those crimes are related to the double homicide investigation. The investigations remain active and ongoing.

Anyone with information about the homicides is asked to contact Crime Stoppers at 662-910-0400. Information may qualify for a cash reward of up to $2,000.

Information leading to Douglas’ arrest may qualify for a reward of up to $1,000. Tips may also be reported to the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411.

item.title: Mississippi insurance commissioner urges residents to review hurricane, flood coverage before storm season - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STATEWIDE — Mississippi Insurance Commissioner Mike Chaney is encouraging residents to review their insurance policies and prepare their homes ahead of hurricane season, especially after recent flooding in parts of the state.

Chaney said while there is no specific “hurricane insurance” policy, homeowners can purchase different types of coverage to protect against storm-related damage.

“Multiple peril insurance is one option that covers wind damage or hail damage caused by a hurricane or other named storms,” Chaney said. “With recent flooding in the Pine Belt and on the Gulf Coast, I hope homeowners will also take a hard look at their flood insurance needs.”

According to the Mississippi Insurance Department, standard homeowners insurance policies generally cover wind and hail damage but do not cover flooding. Flood insurance must typically be purchased separately, often through the National Flood Insurance Program, and usually includes a 30-day waiting period before coverage begins.

State officials said fewer than 50,000 flood insurance policies were active in Mississippi as of December 2025.

Chaney also urged homeowners to speak with their insurance agents about changes in coverage needs and policy details. Officials recommended shopping around for coverage, increasing deductibles, bundling policies and making home improvements to help reduce insurance premiums.

The department also encouraged residents to create a home inventory using the NAIC Home Inventory App to document belongings before severe weather strikes.

Residents with insurance questions or claim issues can contact the Mississippi Insurance Department at 1-800-562-2957 or visit Mississippi Insurance Department.

Chaney said while there is no specific “hurricane insurance” policy, homeowners can purchase different types of coverage to protect against storm-related damage.

“Multiple peril insurance is one option that covers wind damage or hail damage caused by a hurricane or other named storms,” Chaney said. “With recent flooding in the Pine Belt and on the Gulf Coast, I hope homeowners will also take a hard look at their flood insurance needs.”

According to the Mississippi Insurance Department, standard homeowners insurance policies generally cover wind and hail damage but do not cover flooding. Flood insurance must typically be purchased separately, often through the National Flood Insurance Program, and usually includes a 30-day waiting period before coverage begins.

State officials said fewer than 50,000 flood insurance policies were active in Mississippi as of December 2025.

Chaney also urged homeowners to speak with their insurance agents about changes in coverage needs and policy details. Officials recommended shopping around for coverage, increasing deductibles, bundling policies and making home improvements to help reduce insurance premiums.

The department also encouraged residents to create a home inventory using the NAIC Home Inventory App to document belongings before severe weather strikes.

Residents with insurance questions or claim issues can contact the Mississippi Insurance Department at 1-800-562-2957 or visit Mississippi Insurance Department.

item.title: Missing Jackson woman last seen after dropping off daughter, granddaughter - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Jackson Police Department is asking for the public’s help finding a missing woman.

Michelle Parker, 55, was reported missing May 24, according to a public notification issued by police. The notice was dated May 26.

Police said Parker was last seen Friday, May 22, when she dropped off her daughter at work and her granddaughter at school. She was supposed to attend a reporting party’s coordinated placement appointment with Mississippi Sports Medicine at 1325 E. Fortification St., but the reporting party is unsure if Parker made it to work, according to police.

Parker was last seen driving a white Chevrolet Malibu with no tag.

She is described as 5 feet, 7 inches tall and weighing about 140 pounds. She has brown hair, brown eyes and a pixie haircut. Police said she was last seen wearing a blue apron, blue jeans, a T-shirt and tennis shoes.

Parker has been entered into the National Crime Information Center as a missing person.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1800 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS (8477). In a life-threatening emergency, call 911.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Lottie "Elaine" Myers, Franklin County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
FRANKLIN COUNTY — Authorities are still searching for a Pike County woman who disappeared in Franklin County in October 2024 after leaving her home in Summit.

Lottie “Elaine” Myers, 73, was last seen around 1:47 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 28, 2024, in the 2000 block of Willis Cotton Road in Summit.

According to investigators, Myers was driving south in a silver 2015 Jeep Cherokee bearing Mississippi license plate PJ1 091. Her vehicle was later found abandoned on McCall Creek Road in Franklin County.

Authorities believe Myers was later seen walking along McCall Creek Road in an unknown direction.

The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation issued a Silver Alert for Myers on Oct. 29, 2024, noting that she suffers from Alzheimer’s disease, which impairs her judgment.

Myers is described as a white female with brown hair and brown eyes. She is approximately 5 feet 5 inches to 5 feet 6 inches tall and weighs between 150 and 170 pounds. She was last seen wearing faded knee-length blue jean shorts and a gray T-shirt.

Multiple agencies have searched the McCall Creek Road area since Myers disappeared, but she has not been found.

Anyone with information about Myers’ whereabouts is asked to contact the Pike County Sheriff’s Department at (601) 782-2323.
